experiments.title: CPU numerical paths
experiments.description: Scalar references and one- or two-thread optimized calls across three workloads.
experiments.finding: Extra threads and an optimized path can cost more than they save on small inputs. Inspect each workload and size.
experiments.boundary: Completed synchronous native call, including validation, allocation and output disposal.
experiments.excluded: Input generation, Python snapshots, runtime queueing and GPU transfers.
experiments.limitations: Five warm samples, fixed condition order and a shared Windows workstation. First invocation is retained, not a cold-process measurement.

experiments.title: Original CPU / CUDA comparison
experiments.description: The same original complete-call boundary with separate CUDA event intervals.
experiments.finding: CUDA complete-call medians were slower than optimized CPU in every tested condition. Shared bins helped uniform input but hurt concentrated input at the largest size.
experiments.boundary: Validation, allocations, checksum selection and result destruction. CUDA includes upload, launch, download, synchronization and resource cleanup.
experiments.excluded: Input generation, Python conversion and queueing. Device events are separate intervals and are never added to host elapsed time.
experiments.limitations: Five warm samples, fixed condition order and a shared Windows workstation. First invocation is retained, not a cold-process measurement.

experiments.title: CPU stencil dispatch correction
experiments.description: The original and follow-up collections keep the same stencil arithmetic and thread counts.
experiments.finding: Moving AVX2 support detection out of the row loop lowered every listed stencil median in this follow-up. Thread startup still outweighed small work.
experiments.boundary: Same completed native CPU boundary in two separate collections. Original CPU results are not relabelled as a new GPU baseline.
experiments.excluded: Input generation, Python conversion and queueing.
experiments.limitations: Five warm samples, fixed condition order and a shared Windows workstation. First invocation is retained, not a cold-process measurement. Shared-host timing alone does not establish causality.

experiments.title: Histogram resource reuse
experiments.description: Six paths retain both CPU thread counts and global/shared bin methods. Each histogram uses 64 by 64 tiles.
experiments.finding: Small inputs favored CPU. At 1024 by 1024, reused shared bins for uniform input and reused global bins for concentrated input beat the faster tested CPU median.
experiments.boundary: Call entry to an independently owned, usable host result. Both CUDA paths upload current input and synchronize. Simple calls retire resources inside the call.
experiments.excluded: Setup, final retirement, output comparison, checksum and host result destruction. Reused resources survive between calls. This boundary differs from the original study.
experiments.limitations: 24 warm samples per condition, rotated backend order and a shared Windows workstation. Two extra warmups are outside the retained rows. No pinned input, zero-copy or transfer overlap.

experiments.title: CPU inference session reuse
experiments.description: Serial one-image calls through one ONNX session, at application batch sizes 1, 2 and 8.
experiments.finding: Reusing the owner/session lowered repeated call cost. The direct Python CPU session was faster than the C++ wrapper at every tested batch size.
experiments.boundary: Prepared tensors to completed host logits. Fresh C++ calls include session creation, admission, reconciliation and close. Reused setup and retirement are separate.
experiments.excluded: PNG decoding/normalization, reference validation and journal writes. The direct Python baseline lacks the wrapper's request identity and generation accounting.
experiments.limitations: 20 samples after five warmups. First invocation is separate. One-thread CPU configuration on a shared Windows workstation. This is also a wrapper comparison, not a language ranking.

experiments.title: Required CUDA inference
experiments.description: Required CUDA owner/session paths compared with a direct CPU session in the same provider installation.
experiments.finding: The direct Python CPU baseline was faster at all three tested batches. Reuse helped repeated CUDA calls, but setup and retirement still cost time.
experiments.boundary: Prepared tensors to completed host logits. Fresh C++ calls include session creation, admission, reconciliation and close. Reused setup and retirement are separate.
experiments.excluded: PNG decoding/normalization, reference validation and journal writes. The direct Python baseline lacks the wrapper's request identity and generation accounting.
experiments.limitations: 20 samples after five warmups on a shared Windows workstation. Application batches are serial one-image calls, not fused GPU batching. Operator events prove placement, not kernel timing or overlap.
